teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji edge Italy 21-16 for first Nations Championship win
teams.body: Saturday's Round 6 meeting at the Bluenergy Stadium in Udine closed the pool stage for both sides. White's men arrived winless, having faded after half-time in a 43-15 defeat by Ireland, a pattern the Italian federation said had recurred through the tournament. Italy were disrupted before kickoff: tighthead Simone Ferrari injured his left arm an hour out, so Marco Riccioni was promoted from the bench and Ion Neculai took the No. 18 shirt.

teams.heading: Henry Slade opens scoring as England rout All Blacks by record margin
teams.body: Fin Smith's grubber put Slade over after four minutes of Saturday's 37-12 win at Allianz Stadium, and further tries from Jack van Poortvliet and Ben Earl had England 19-0 up after 36 minutes. Ollie Chessum smashed over for the fourth soon after the restart, all without winger Tommy Freeman, an injury withdrawal before kick-off. Planet Rugby notes the 25-point margin eclipses England's 38-21 win of 2012; the Guardian calls it New Zealand's heaviest defeat by any northern hemisphere nation.

lead.why: England's record win over the All Blacks is the day's biggest England event not already run.

teams.heading: French federation arranges Aramburu tribute, Antoine Dupont to escort his son
teams.body: The Fédération française de rugby organised a tribute for Saturday's France-Argentina match at the Stade de France to Federico Martin Aramburu, the former Argentina player well known in the French championship in the early 2000s. He was murdered in Paris in 2022 by two far-right activists, sentenced to 26 and 19 years. Supporters were to hold a minute's applause. According to the FFR, his son would walk out in an Argentina shirt, holding the hands of Antoine Dupont and Julian Montoya, honouring his dual nationality.

lead.why: The Gros injury and Duzan preview have already run, so the FFR's tribute plan, with Dupont's role in it, is the freshest France event.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell asks if suspended Rassie Erasmus was 'drinking whiskey' on livestream
teams.body: Ireland's head coach had the last laugh after Saturday's 20-17 win over South Africa. Rassie Erasmus, suspended by World Rugby over his comments about match officials, missed the game and instead hosted a livestream from the team hotel, open only to registered viewers aged 18 and over. Asked about it at his post-match press conference, Farrell laughed: "Then why was it 18 and over then? Was he drinking whiskey or something?!" He added that the Springboks later joined Ireland's dressing room for a beer.

lead.why: Farrell's jibe at the suspended Erasmus is the freshest Ireland talking point and is distinct from the match report already run.

teams.heading: Quesada says wing injuries pushed Capuozzo wide to start Miotti against Fiji
teams.body: Domingo Miotti was named at fly-half for Saturday's 16-21 defeat by Fiji in Udine after Gonzalo Quesada chose not to ease him in from the bench. At Thursday's team announcement, Quesada said he had weighed Paolo Garbisi or Tommaso Allan at 10, with Miotti among the replacements and Ange Capuozzo at full-back, but injuries to wingers — Lynagh, Faissal, Pani and Trulla — made shifting Capuozzo wide, with Allan at full-back, the better fit. He added that debuting a key-position player from the start is, paradoxically, easier.

lead.why: NEW #1 is the Ferrari late withdrawal, which already ran today with no new development, so Quesada's explanation of the Miotti selection is the strongest unrun Italy story.

teams.heading: Liam McConnell scores hat-trick on third Scotland appearance in Japan rout
teams.body: The 22-year-old Edinburgh back-rower ran in all three tries before the hour of Saturday's 67-5 Nations Championship win over Japan at Murrayfield. BBC Scotland's Tom English noted the frustration among his supporters at his lack of Scotland opportunities. His second try came early in the second half from Darcy Graham's kick-and-chase and offload. Graham matched him with a hat-trick of his own, taking his Scotland try record to 41 in an 11-try afternoon.

lead.why: McConnell's hat-trick on only his third cap is the fresh Scotland story from the Japan rout and a different angle from the Townsend points-blitz edition.

teams.heading: Wales haka response draws 1.1 million YouTube views in six days
teams.body: The Dragon's breath effect that met the haka in Cardiff had been a year in the making, El-Balad reports, built to answer the ritual with something theatrical and unmistakably Welsh. ITV's footage of it drew 1.1 million hits on YouTube inside six days. The same piece contrasts it with Twickenham, where England fans were expected to try to drown out the haka with Swing Low, Sweet Chariot — a familiar tactic, it argues, beside a one-off show that took time, planning and imagination.

lead.why: It is the only new, Wales-centred item; the WRU and Tandy stories have already run, and the broadcast item is logistics.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards brought Pumas defence to Saint-Denis against France side he coached
teams.body: Edwards spent six years running France's defence until the French federation ended his contract before the summer. Rugbyrama's Nicolas Zanardi doubted he had dropped his core principles for Saturday's Nations Championship meeting at the Stade de France: a 13-man first line, 14 inside the last 20 metres, double tackles to kill offloads and no easy rucks. France lineout coach Laurent Sempéré said in the week that both sides had evolved, Edwards included, as he adapted to new colleagues. Zanardi pointed to flaws France know well, notably forward circulation after lineouts.

lead.why: Fresh Argentina-centred story: the Pumas' defence coach taking his system against the France side he drilled for six years.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson captained Wallabies in Cardiff with Carter Gordon at fly-half
teams.body: Australia named Wilson at No. 8 for Saturday's round-six Nations Championship test against Wales at the Principality Stadium, with Gordon outside Ryan Lonergan. Fraser McReight was among the replacements on a five-three bench, leaving Carlo Tizzano at openside and Rob Valetini on the blindside. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Len Ikitau formed the midfield behind a front row of Isaac Kailea, Brandon Paenga-Amosa and Taniela Tupou. Wales came in off their first win over New Zealand in 73 years, and France's Luc Ramos refereed.

teams.heading: Takuro Matsunaga scores Japan's lone try; Harada and Stolberg sin-binned at Murrayfield
teams.body: Saturday's 67-5 defeat had one bright moment for Japan. In the 53rd minute a Scotland box kick bounced awkwardly past Kyle Rowe, and Takuro Matsunaga took an unconverted try, the visitors' only points. Planet Rugby reports that discipline then frayed late on. Mamoru Harada was yellow-carded for a 69th-minute hip drop, and Michael Stolberg for an early tackle in the 79th. Eddie Jones had made wholesale changes after the England defeat, fielding what the BBC called a severely weakened team.

teams.heading: All Blacks slump to record 37-12 defeat by England at Twickenham
teams.body: England's 25-point margin beat their previous best against New Zealand, the 38-21 win at Twickenham in 2012, and came a week after the 35-28 loss to Wales. Ethan de Groot's try was all Dave Rennie's side had by half-time, trailing 19-5. Beauden Barrett marked his 150th Test with a score converted by Damian McKenzie, but England's bench took over. The defeat left the Springboks needing one log point against Ireland in Dublin to top the southern hemisphere standings and reach the final.

lead.why: The weekend's result is the most widely covered New Zealand story, and it is a fresh event rather than the Meagher column already run.

teams.heading: Springboks beaten 20-17 by Ireland in Dublin with banned Erasmus absent
teams.body: Saturday's sixth-round Nations Championship Test at the Aviva Stadium capped a week that began with defeat in France and ended without Rassie Erasmus, absent while serving a six-match ban that his union has challenged by requesting a full misconduct hearing. Christophe Ridley refereed what Rugbyrama called an incredible Irish victory. SA Rugby Magazine's verdict was blunter, branding the Boks wasteful and Ireland cunning. South Africa sit third of 12 on the log after six games, four of them won.

lead.why: The result in Dublin is the day's hard South Africa event; the watchalong has already run and the rest is opinion.
